requirements.quote: I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

requirements.text: The requested scope includes generated resolver cache and helper types, not only the outer formatter and resolver declarations.

claims.statement: Integer-keyed object formatter generation places the fully qualified exclusion attribute on the formatter class inside the NETSTANDARD2_0/NETFRAMEWORK preprocessor guard.
String-keyed formatter generation applies the same guarded exclusion attribute to its formatter class in both the T4 template and checked-in template output.
Enum formatter generation decorates the generated formatter class with the guarded exclusion attribute.
The checked-in union template output decorates the union formatter class with the guarded exclusion attribute.
GeneratedMessagePackResolver output decorates three declarations: the resolver class, its nested FormatterCache<T>, and its nested GetFormatterHelper class.
Composite resolver output decorates both the outer resolver class and its nested FormatterCache<T> class with guarded exclusion attributes.

The new tests run the generator over declared object, string-keyed object, enum, union, and resolver inputs, require at least five generated files, assert at least one exclusion attribute in every returned file, and count only the two supported guarded attribute layouts as guarded occurrences.
When a generated nesting type has generic constraints, the nesting utility now emits a newline after its opening brace, separating that brace from subsequent generated declarations.

The updated expected-output resources contain the new guarded decorations and agree with the head generator for the changed snapshot-based tests, while those tests discriminate against output produced with the base generator source.
README documentation describes formatter and resolver decoration and explicitly documents netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework as conditional exceptions.

citations.quote:
All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, so generated code does not skew code coverage reports.
The attribute is only emitted for targets where it is available (not `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework).

claims.statement: The exclusion behavior is added without a new public configuration API; the public-surface check reports no changed public declaration, public API entry, or diagnostic ID.

decisions.statement: The implementation chooses textual preprocessor guards, so the attribute is inactive when NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK is defined, instead of pursuing unconditional decoration on every target.
decisions.whyHuman: Compilation experiments can establish where the attribute exists and whether a candidate output compiles, but they cannot decide whether the requirement's unqualified 'all generated code' scope should yield to target compatibility, or which compatibility mechanism consumers should receive. The added tests assert the chosen guard rather than settling that product choice.
options: Emit the attribute under #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK, as implemented.
Emit the attribute unconditionally for every target under a literal reading of the request.
Inspect each consumer compilation for the attribute type and generate target-specific output rather than emitting preprocessor branches.
Use a compatibility declaration or polyfill for targets lacking the framework attribute, subject to avoiding type conflicts.

citations.quote: The attribute is only emitted for targets where it is available (not `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework).

decisions.statement: The change implements always-on generation without an opt-in or opt-out setting.
decisions.whyHuman: The requirement explicitly accepts both no setting and a setting. Tests can verify either behavior but cannot determine which configuration experience the owners want.
options: No setting; always generate the guarded decoration, as implemented.
Add an opt-out setting with decoration enabled by default.
Add an opt-in setting with decoration disabled by default.

decisions.statement: The decoration granularity includes concrete generated formatters, resolvers, caches, and helper classes, but not the partial nesting/container type declarations emitted to host generated code.
decisions.whyHuman: The phrase 'all generated code' does not define whether empty generated partial declarations for user types count as independently excludable code. Decorating such a partial user type can also affect coverage attribution for its user-written parts. A textual test cannot settle that scope decision.
options: Decorate concrete generated formatter/resolver/helper types but not generated user-type nesting declarations, as implemented.
Also decorate generated partial nesting/container declarations and accept their whole-type coverage semantics.
Decorate only outer generated formatter/resolver classes and omit separate nested helper decorations.

findings.statement: The union formatter decoration is present in checked-in UnionTemplate.cs, but the supplied diff has no corresponding UnionTemplate.tt change. Unlike the other edited template outputs, the source template is not shown to reproduce this output; if it does not already contain equivalent text, a future T4 regeneration will drop the union decoration. No template-regeneration check is included in the evidence.

AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage does not test every generated type: it checks only whether each file contains the attribute at least once. The nesting utility emits partial type declarations without an exclusion attribute, so a file can contain such an undecorated declaration and still pass whenever another declaration in that file has the attribute. This leaves the test's stated per-type guarantee unsupported even though decorating user partial containers is itself a separate scope decision.

ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable does not compile either preprocessor configuration named by the test. It normalizes and counts strings after one generator run using default references; it supplies no NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK parse options and checks no compilation diagnostics. Guard-specific syntax errors or attribute-resolution failures can therefore remain undetected.

The new tests do not enforce the generated category set described by their own comment. The only cardinality assertion is generated.Count >= 5, followed by assertions over whatever files happen to be returned; no assertion requires an enum formatter, a union formatter, both object formatter variants, and a resolver by path. A category omitted by the generator is not directly detected if at least five other files remain.
